set_text.text: Food markup is what you add to the cost of food product to set its selling price. For a distributor that cuts, trims or portions product, that cost has to sit on the pounds that sell. Trim is paid for but does not sell at the cut's price.
The pounds that leave on an invoice. A 40 lb case at an 85% yield gives 34 lb, and the full $48.00 has to come back from those 34.
Cutting labor and packaging. The $48.00 landed cost covers freight and handling in, not the hours on the saw, so the margin has to pay for them.
Catch-weight items are billed by the pound, so a light case also costs less. The price per usable lb holds whatever a case weighs, as long as the yield holds.
Who uses a food markup calculator
It is built for independent food distributors that cut, trim or portion product in-house. Anyone who prices a cut item, sets a yield standard or manages cutters should run it.
